summary: Embedding ingest produced duplicate internal IDs (hash collisions) resulting in reranker returning duplicate top-k and increased latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexaSearch reports that after a nightly bulk embed upload, reranker queries return duplicate documents in the top-k and end-to-end query latency spikes by ~3-6x for affected queries. Behavior started after a large bulk ingest (1.2M rows) on 2026-03-09.

Impact:
- Duplicate top-k results (same doc_id appears multiple times in results) causing poor UX for LexaSearch customers.
- Elevated rerank/recall latency for affected queries (p95 downstream latency from 120ms -> 450-700ms).
- Intermittent 503s observed in rerank service when merging duplicates under load.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east (dedicated for enterprise customers)
- Ingest pipeline: ingest-service v3.6.1 -> transform -> shard-write -> indexer
- Embedding model: embed-large-v2 (fp16 quant path)
- Reranker: rerank-light-v1 running on dedicated pool

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Upload bulk file via /v1/embeddings/bulk with payload containing 'doc_id' as alphanumeric strings: many short user-generated IDs (~8 chars).
2) Wait for indexing job to complete (indexer logs show completed for job 2026-03-09T02:00Z).
3) Run rerank query against rerank endpoint /v1/rerank with query ids that target the uploaded corpus.
4) Observe duplicate document entries in returned top-k and higher latency.

Observed behavior:
- Internal IDs in embeddings store show collisions: two different doc_id values mapped to the same internal_id (internal_id hashes identical).
- Reranker merge step returns duplicates because it indexes by internal_id; dedup logic is shallow and does not detect near-duplicate vectors.
- Indexer logs contain repeated warnings: "WARN indexer: duplicate internal_id detected, overwriting entry" around 2026-03-09T01:58:44Z.
- Dashboard: shard-12 write QPS spike and indexer GC increased during re-ingest (link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/ingest/dash?shard=12).

Expected behavior:
- Each uploaded embedding retains uniqueness; internal_id should be collision-resistant for customer-provided doc_id values.
- Reranker should not produce duplicate top-k entries for distinct documents.

Relevant logs / excerpts:
- indexer.log snippet:
  [2026-03-09T01:58:44Z] WARN indexer shard-12 duplicate internal_id=0x4f3a9b2c for src_doc_id=AB12 and src_doc_id=Q9X7
  [2026-03-09T01:58:45Z] INFO indexer shard-12 overwrite completed
- rerank service trace: trace_id=trc-9f8a3, p95_merge=610ms, merge_retries=3

Initial hypothesis:
- ingest-service uses a 64-bit non-cryptographic hash (murmur3_64) over doc_id for internal_id storage. At large scale with many short user-provided IDs there is a non-negligible probability of collisions. The duplicate internal_ids cause overwrites at index time and duplicate entries at query time.
- Dedup behavior in rerank expects dedupe by metadata and does not handle collisions at the internal_id layer.

Requested from customer:
- Full sample of original upload (already provided as anonymized CSV).
- Confirmation whether they use short, low-entropy doc_id values (customer confirmed ~80% of ids are 6-9 chars with limited alphabet).

Next steps planned: validate collision probability on current hashing strategy and implement mitigations (see investigation_notes).
comments: Support - 2026-03-10: Thanks for the report, LexaSearch. We've escalated to SRE and Ingest owners. Can you share a sanitized sample of the uploaded CSV and a job_id?
Customer (LexaSearch) - 2026-03-10: Provided sample and job_id ingest-20260309-58. They confirm doc_id pattern: [A-Z0-9]{6,9} with heavy reuse of short prefixes.

SRE (Tomás Rivera) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally by fuzzing 6-9 char ids; murmur3_64 produced collisions at scale in our test harness (collision rate ~1 in 250k with this id distribution). Created reproduction job rep-20260311 on staging.

Support (Aisha Kumar) - 2026-03-11: Noted that indexer log contains explicit duplicate internal_id warnings. Raised ingest-service PR to add collision detection: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-service/pull/4298
Customer (LexaSearch) - 2026-03-12: Impact: duplicate results are actively surfacing in production and causing product complaints. They request a hotfix and a timeline for a permanent fix.

SRE (Tomás Rivera) - 2026-03-12: Applied temporary mitigation for LexaSearch: backfill job that re-wrote internal_ids by appending a short salt derived from upload timestamp for colliding entries. Deploying change to indexer-dedup-worker in us-east canary now. Monitoring for latency improvement.

Support - 2026-03-13: Can confirm customer saw reduced duplicate-topk in canary traffic (sampled queries show duplicates reduced from 12% to 0.8%). Still tracking stability and preparing a permanent ingest fix.
investigation_notes: Reproduction: used a generator for 1.5M doc_ids with distribution matching customer sample; murmur3_64 collisions reproduced. Collision analysis: collisions cluster when doc_ids have low entropy and short length. Short-term mitigation options evaluated: (1) switch to 128-bit salted hash (xxh3_128) at ingest-time, (2) fallback to salted UUID when collision detected, (3) add post-write validation that checks for multiple distinct source doc_ids mapping to same internal_id and mark for re-ingest. We implemented option (2) as hotfix for this customer and are implementing option (1) as permanent fix in ingest-service v3.6.2. Also flagged rerank dedupe logic for improvement to detect duplicate vectors beyond internal_id equality.
workaround: Hotfix applied: ingest-worker backfill that detects internal_id collisions and rewrites colliding entries with a deterministic salt (upload timestamp + monotonic counter). Canary run for LexaSearch reduced duplicate-topk from ~12% -> <1%. Hotfix link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-service/pull/4298. Temporary mitigation will remain until ingest-service v3.6.2 rollout.
next_steps:
1) Finish ingest-service v3.6.2 change to use xxh3_128 for internal_id generation and add unit tests for collision detection (owner: ingest-team, ETA: 2026-03-18).
2) Harden rerank dedupe to check vector similarity if multiple results share internal_id or metadata (owner: rerank-team, ETA: 2026-03-20).
3) Run a one-off global scan for collisions for enterprise customers who used bulk uploads in last 30 days and schedule targeted backfills (owner: support-sre, ETA: 2026-03-22).
4) Postmortem and playbook update (owner: support-ops, ETA: 2026-03-25).
public_communication: We will notify LexaSearch with a timeline for permanent fix and confirm when the global scan/backfill is complete. No customer-facing incident page created at this time; internal customers impacted only.
